title: Research: sharp four-XOR cost for the ten-query common-map connector
body:
PR1340's ten-query common-B connector uses twelve complete source XORs. This contribution reduces that count to **four and proves four is the generic minimum**, retaining exactly ten B queries, two readouts for each of the 31 masks, and restoration of every arbitrary dirty source/connector/scratch row. Under its abstract complete tariff, the bill falls from **2760 to 2744**. This is a scoped recursive-interface result; no new kappa or physical supplier adoption is claimed.

The lower bound projects words with fewer than four source XORs onto their source-restoration map. The only nonempty restored subsequences are two identical XORs; connector parity reduces every full-span ten-query case to the retained 945-pairing obstruction. The four-XOR path derives from Ross Richardson's PR943 twelve-toggle repair by omitting two boundaries. See `research/mutable-source-shear-cost/PROOF.md` for the complete quantifiers, reduction, price conditions and limits.

Validation on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12.14 and 3.14.7:

- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mutable-source-shear-cost` passes, including six package test groups.
- The separate checker imports no primary code. Row/column engines agree on all 8421 short source words; direct differences and matching/Walsh engines agree on all 945 pairing records. Full free noncommutative root/recursive/inverse maps cover all 40 arbitrary incoming rows; the separate dense oracle checks 3456 executions at L=1,2,3,4.
- Seven semantic controls, eight on-disk corruptions, optimized read-only relocation, deterministic export, source pins, selected-record integrity and whitespace checks pass.

Base: current main `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. PR1340 is pinned at `f1dcab36fa63f8226f70dd07e26f44afb9d39b51`; its three retained source files are byte-identical and no pending executable is imported. Final overlap coverage: 837 open PRs including drafts, 87 Discussion records, 327 local notes/metadata/ledger records, complete pagination, no warnings. Task/claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1352.

The common exact F2-linear B, temporarily writable unobserved source rows, paired readouts and complete-call contracts are essential. Specialized operators may be cheaper. No weighted global optimum, selected cold replay, native compiler/owner admission, physical frame/precision/tape admission, all-size outer transfer or proof-assistant theorem is claimed. Only this scoped research directory is added; the selected frontier is unchanged.

Credit Arham Tahir's PR1340 for the mutable-source extension, query minimum and tariff; Ross Richardson's PR943/934 for the universal obstruction/repair and dirty recursive lowering; shhxera/CubeJerry's PR889 and Chafik Boukhalfa's PR628 for the retained batching/commutator lineage. Original source notices and cumulative repository credit remain. Prepared by Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, algebra, both implementations, tests and writing; no subagents or independent human review. Apache-2.0.
